waypoints.name: Goodell Creek / Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (SR-20, Newhalem)
waypoints.note: Unpaved turnout off SR-20 across from Newhalem, signed for Goodell Creek; no parking pass is needed, but an overnight trip needs a wilderness permit from the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
waypoints.directions: The trailhead is an unpaved turnout off SR-20 across from Newhalem, signed for Goodell Creek. No parking pass is needed here, but camping in the Terror or Crescent Creek basins needs a wilderness permit, issued in person at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.

waypoints.name: Upper trail fork
waypoints.note: Maintained forestry-road-bed trail ends here; climbers' path continues with diminishing cairns/flagging toward Terror Creek.
waypoints.directions: Follow the old, overgrown Goodell Creek logging road up the valley for about 3.5 miles to the fork where the road tread ends and a cairned climbers' path continues toward Terror Creek.

waypoints.name: Terror Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Ford Terror Creek at a shallow braid; crossing depth is very flow-dependent and can be a wade in high water.

waypoints.name: The Barrier
waypoints.note: Steep, brushy, loose ridge (spur off Mt. Degenhardt) separating Terror Creek and Crescent Creek basins; cross via a loose ledge system near the lower Terror Glacier or a higher moat crossing below Degenhardt — classic sustained 'Pickets Class 3' that turns parties back.

waypoints.name: Crescent Creek Basin camp (below Mt. Terror)
waypoints.note: Established high camp on a flat bench below Mount Terror with meltwater from two overhead slab streams; the basin runs 6,050–6,440 ft.

waypoints.name: Eye Col gully traverse
waypoints.note: Drop ~300 ft below the moraine to Crescent Creek's head, then rising-traverse below the Eye Col gully past an adjacent buttress on a minor rib to a notch, avoiding a closed chimney and loose choss.
waypoints.directions: From camp, drop about 300 feet below the moraine to the head of Crescent Creek, then make a rising traverse beneath the gully system on the peak's south side, past the buttress that divides it. Avoid the right-hand gully, which ends in a closed chimney; take the minor rib on its climber's left and pitch through the chockstones in the gully above to the Eye Col notch at about 7,400 feet.

waypoints.name: West Twin Needle
waypoints.note: Above the Eye Col, a 5.7 pitch up white slabs on the east face, then scrambling to the true summit; descend via rappels off the Himmelhorn–West Twin Needle col.
waypoints.directions: From the Eye Col, climb a 5.7 pitch up the white slabs on the east face, then scramble the easier ground above to the true summit.
